hints: Factor the quadratic $(t - 2)(t - 20) = 0$ to find the two positive values of $t$.
walkthrough:
Set velocity to zero to find the instants of rest:
$$-0.01t^3 + 0.22t^2 - 0.4t = 0$$

State the two positive values of $t$:
$$t = 2\text{ s} \quad \text{and} \quad t = 20\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
A particle is instantaneously at rest when its velocity is zero ($v = 0$):
$$-0.01t^3 + 0.22t^2 - 0.4t = 0$$

Find two numbers that multiply to $+40$ and add to $-22$. These numbers are $-2$ and $-20$:
$$-0.01t(t - 2)(t - 20) = 0$$

The roots are $t = 0$, $t = 2$, and $t = 20$. The two positive values are:
$$t = 2\text{ s} \quad \text{and} \quad t = 20\text{ s}$$

hints: To maximize acceleration, differentiate $a(t)$ with respect to $t$ and set equal to zero: $\frac{da}{dt} = -0.06t + 0.44 = 0$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate acceleration with respect to time to find turning points:
$$\frac{da}{dt} = -0.06t + 0.44 = 0$$
teacher_walkthrough:
First, find acceleration by differentiating the velocity function $v(t) = -0.01t^3 + 0.22t^2 - 0.4t$:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = -0.03t^2 + 0.44t - 0.4$$

To find when acceleration is greatest, find the stationary point of $a(t)$ by differentiating with respect to $t$:
$$\frac{da}{dt} = -0.06t + 0.44$$

Set the derivative to zero:
$$-0.06t + 0.44 = 0$$
$$0.06t = 0.44$$
$$t = \frac{0.44}{0.06} = \frac{44}{6} = \frac{22}{3}\text{ s} \approx 7.33\text{ s}$$
Verify this is a maximum using the second derivative: $\frac{d^2a}{dt^2} = -0.06 < 0$, confirming maximum acceleration at $t = \frac{22}{3}\text{ s}$.

hints: From part (i), velocity is positive in the interval $2 < t < 20$.
Evaluate $s(20) - s(2)$ using $s(t) = -0.0025t^4 + \frac{0.22}{3}t^3 - 0.2t^2$ to find the distance.
walkthrough: Identify that velocity is positive for $2 < t < 20$ from the roots found in part (i).

Integrate velocity with respect to time to find displacement:
$$s(t) = \int (-0.01t^3 + 0.22t^2 - 0.4t)\,dt = -\frac{0.01}{4}t^4 + \frac{0.22}{3}t^3 - 0.2t^2 = -0.0025t^4 + \frac{0.22}{3}t^3 - 0.2t^2$$

Calculate total distance travelled:
$$\text{Distance} = s(20) - s(2) = \frac{320}{3} - \left(-\frac{0.76}{3}\right) = \frac{320.76}{3} = 106.92\text{ m} \approx 107\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Velocity is positive when $2 < t < 20$. Because velocity does not change sign on this open interval, distance equals displacement:

Find the indefinite integral of velocity with respect to time:
$$s(t) = \int (-0.01t^3 + 0.22t^2 - 0.4t)dt = -\frac{0.01t^4}{4} + \frac{0.22t^3}{3} - \frac{0.4t^2}{2} + C$$
$$s(t) = -0.0025t^4 + \frac{0.22}{3}t^3 - 0.2t^2 + C$$

Subtract the lower limit from the upper limit:
$$\text{Distance} = s(20) - s(2) = \frac{320}{3} - \left(-\frac{0.76}{3}\right) = \frac{320.76}{3} = 106.92\text{ m} = \frac{2673}{25}\text{ m} \approx 107\text{ m}$$
